universal_lens: Time series forecasting via ARIMA-RNN ensembles integrates historical player performance with linear programming for optimal fantasy team construction under budget and positional constraints. primitives.name: Hybrid Time Series Forecasting Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: This study aims to tackle this problem by using a hybrid of Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) for time series prediction of player points and subsequent maximisation of total points using Linear Programming (LPP).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Y_t': 'Player points at time t (dimensionless)', 'ARIMA(p,d,q)': 'Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average model parameters', 'RNN(h)': 'Recurrent Neural Network hidden state vector'}
primitives.assumptions: Player performance follows stationary stochastic processes; ensemble of ARIMA and RNN captures linear and nonlinear temporal dependencies.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When historical data insufficient or noisy, model convergence degrades.

layer2.mapping: GSI's predictive kernel derives forecast distributions from ARIMA-RNN ensembles; GSE's decision layer applies LPP to select optimal player combinations.
layer2.telemetry: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of point predictions vs actual performance.

primitives.name: Linear Programming Team Optimization
primitives.verbatim_quote: Constraints on the types of players like goalkeepers, defenders, midfielders and forwards along with the total budget were effectively optimised using LPP approach.
primitives.latex: \max \sum_{i=1}^{n} c_i x_i \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \sum_{i=1}^{n} w_i x_i \leq B, \quad A x \leq b
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'c_i': 'Points contribution of player i (dimensionless)', 'x_i': 'Binary variable indicating player i inclusion (dimensionless)', 'w_i': 'Cost of player i (£Million)', 'B': 'Total budget (£Million)', 'A': 'Constraint matrix (player type counts)', 'b': 'Player count limits per role'}
primitives.assumptions: Player point contributions are deterministic within forecast range; team composition adheres to fixed positional and budgetary rules.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When constraint set is infeasible due to high-value player scarcity.

layer2.mapping: GSI’s optimization module mirrors LPP structure; GSE translates into action-state transitions for real-time team adjustments.
layer2.telemetry: Optimal team score achieved vs baseline random selection.

primitives.name: Ensemble Prediction Framework
primitives.verbatim_quote: Given the player points for the past three seasons, the predictions have been made for the current season by modelling differently for ARIMA and RNN, and then creating an ensemble of the same.
primitives.assumptions: Individual models are independently accurate; ensemble improves generalization via averaging.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When ARIMA and RNN outputs diverge beyond tolerance thresholds.

layer2.mapping: GSI’s ensemble kernel aggregates ARIMA and RNN forecasts; GSE uses variance-weighted average for adaptive forecasting.
layer2.telemetry: Variance reduction in prediction error post-ensembling.

primitives.name: Data Preprocessing Pipeline

primitives.assumptions: Input data contains noise and outliers; normalization and scaling improve model stability.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When data distribution shifts significantly from training period.

layer2.mapping: GSI’s preprocessing pipeline aligns with standard ML pipelines; GSE applies feature engineering for contextual state representation.

primitives.name: Player Metadata Mapping Operator

primitives.assumptions: Players are uniquely identifiable by name and team; cost is normalized to millions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When P > 584 or C < 0, data integrity is compromised.

layer2.mapping: Maps player attributes to GSI probabilistic model nodes for value estimation.
layer2.telemetry: Player attribute consistency check via cross-referenced Kaggle datasets.

primitives.name: Historical Performance Time Series

primitives.assumptions: Points accumulate linearly; missing gameweeks indicate player absence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When t > 38 or PID not found, time-series continuity fails.

layer2.mapping: Generates kernel density estimates for player performance trends over time.
layer2.telemetry: Validation against official FPL gameweek logs.

primitives.name: Noisy Data Correction Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Data The data utilised in the research was collected from the official Fantasy Premier League website [18] which has all the details about various players taking part in the English Premier League for the past five to six years.
primitives.assumptions: Data originates from heterogeneous sources; missing entries are uniformly distributed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When N > 10% of D, data quality threshold breached.

layer2.mapping: Applies conformal correction to D using Han's noise resilience principle.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-validation score between original and cleaned datasets.

primitives.name: Interseason Player Identifier
primitives.verbatim_quote: PID has been provided for correct identification of the same player who has played for different clubs across various seasons.
primitives.assumptions: PID remains constant across teams and seasons; team changes are tracked.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When PID duplicates across S, identity collision occurs.

layer2.mapping: Enables GSE state transition tracking across player career arcs.
layer2.telemetry: Consistency check via FPL API and Kaggle kernel alignment.

primitives.name: Linear Programming (LP)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Linear Optimisation Commonly known as Linear Programming (LP), this seeks to achieve the best outcome in a mathematical model whose requirements are represented by linear relationships.
primitives.assumptions: All relationships between variables are linear; the objective function and constraints are linear expressions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-linearities or non-convexities in the feasible region can cause LP solvers to fail to find global optima.

layer2.mapping: In GSI, LP maps to portfolio optimization under linear risk factors, where the objective is to maximize expected returns subject to budget and exposure constraints. In GSE, it maps to Markov decision processes with linear transition dynamics, optimizing action sequences under state constraints.
layer2.telemetry: For GSI: tracking the Sharpe ratio of optimized portfolios versus benchmarks. For GSE: measuring the cumulative reward achieved by policy derived from LP approximations.

primitives.name: Objective Function
primitives.verbatim_quote: An objective function is maximised or minimised, with respect to certain constraints which vary from situation to situation.
primitives.assumptions: The objective must be quantifiable and expressed as a linear combination of decision variables.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If the objective is non-differentiable or multi-modal, standard LP methods become inapplicable.

layer2.mapping: In GSI, the objective function corresponds to the risk-adjusted return metric (e.g., mean-variance utility). In GSE, it represents the cumulative discounted reward that an agent aims to optimize over a trajectory.
layer2.telemetry: For GSI: realized portfolio variance and excess returns. For GSE: episode rewards and state-value function estimates.

primitives.name: Team Selection Optimization
primitives.verbatim_quote: Once the predicted points for all 326 players were obtained as explained in 4.2, there was a need to maximise the total points for the desired dream team of 15 players.
primitives.assumptions: Predicted points are accurate; player costs are fixed; exactly 15 players are selected without replacement.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When the roster size is small relative to the pool, combinatorial explosion makes exact LP solutions computationally prohibitive.

layer2.mapping: This is a knapsack-constrained LP kernel applied to roster construction, where the 'value' is projected fantasy points and the 'weight' is player cost.
layer2.telemetry: Total predicted vs. actual fantasy points scored by the selected squad, adjusted for budget utilization.

primitives.name: Pulp Library Implementation
primitives.verbatim_quote: The ​Pulp library of Python 2.7 was used for applying the concepts of LPP.
primitives.assumptions: The Pulp interface correctly translates high-level LP specifications into solver input formats.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Solver backend failures occur when the problem instance exceeds memory limits or contains numerical instability.

layer2.telemetry: Solver runtime per optimization problem, convergence status, and solution quality metrics.

primitives.name: Cost-Point Index
